program_name: Master in Energy Engineering (Italian: Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Energetica; German: Master in Energiewissenschaften und -technik). Officially presented on the programme page and in both 2026/27 PDFs simply as 'Master in Energy Engineering', delivered by the Faculty of Engineering of the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano (unibz) 'In collaboration with the University of Trento' (UniTrento). unibz's own ranking-list index files it under the heading 'Inter-university Masters', and the Admission Committee formally includes a UniTrento member (Prof. Alessandro Prada in the Early Bird session; Dr. Vittoria Benedetti in the Late session), with unibz's Prof. Giovanni Pernigotto as President and Degree Course Director. [uncertain] Whether the final parchment is a single jointly-awarded degree, a double degree, or a unibz degree with a UniTrento collaboration note is NOT stated on any unibz.it page checked; the unibz-side wording is only 'In collaboration with the University of Trento'.
level: Master (Italian 'laurea magistrale', second-cycle degree, EQF level 7). 120 ECTS over 2 years, degree class LM-30. Entry qualification is a bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS that gives access to a master programme; the degree opens access to PhD programmes (unibz runs a directly related PhD in Sustainable Energy and Technologies).
teaching_language: FULLY ENGLISH-TAUGHT — this is NOT one of unibz's trilingual programmes. Brochure 'At a glance' box, verbatim: 'Courses will be taught in English (Optional courses could be offered also in Italian and German)'. The admission-information PDF states: 'The official teaching language is English.' Consequence: the only language required for admission is English at B2, and there is NO German or Italian requirement at entry OR at graduation. The Italian/German note applies only to OPTIONAL (elective) courses, so a candidate who speaks no German or Italian can complete the whole 120 ECTS in English by choosing English-taught electives. Because part of the programme is delivered with the University of Trento, students should expect an Italian-speaking environment outside the classroom in Trento (Trentino is monolingual Italian, unlike bilingual Bolzano), but this is a practical/daily-life factor, not a curricular requirement.
campus: Two cities, two universities. Brochure 'At a glance': 'Campus: NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano and Trento'. (1) NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano — unibz's Faculty of Engineering campus in the NOI Techpark science-and-innovation park (Via A. Volta 13/A, Bolzano), the same campus as the Bachelor in Computer Science, Electronic and Information Engineering and Industrial and Mechanical Engineering; the Faculty of Engineering's administrative seat is at Via B. Buozzi 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano. (2) Trento — University of Trento facilities; the brochure's 'Hands-on Experience' list places several site visits in the Trento province (Melinda construction site in Val di Non, HVAC systems of Povo and Mesiano, Dolomiti Energia hydroelectric plant at Castel Tesino), alongside the Zoccolo Dam in South Tyrol managed by Alperia. Bolzano and Trento are about 60 km / roughly 35-50 minutes apart by regional train, so commuting between the two is feasible but is a real logistical/housing factor. [uncertain] The exact split of teaching between the two campuses (which semester or which curriculum sits in Bolzano vs Trento, and how many ECTS are delivered on each site) is not published on the unibz programme page; the 'Study course structure' widget on the page loads dynamically and returned no static course list.
degree_class: LM-30 — 'Ingegneria energetica e nucleare' (Energy and Nuclear Engineering), the Italian ministerial second-cycle degree class. Stated verbatim in the brochure 'At a glance' box: 'Degree class: LM-30'. Practical consequence stated in the admission PDF: 'According to national regulations, simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of two programmes is allowed. However, the two programmes must not belong to the same class, e.g., LM-30/LM-30.' The signed ranking lists add that two simultaneously-enrolled programmes 'must differ for at least 2/3 of the course activities'. Note for Turkish applicants: LM-30 is the class that Italian professional-recognition bodies map to energy/nuclear engineering, which matters for later registration with the Italian engineers' register (Albo degli Ingegneri).
offered_in_2026_27: YES — actively offered and already fully run for 2026/27. This is confirmed at the strongest possible evidential level: unibz has published BOTH signed 2026/27 admission ranking lists for this programme (Early Bird, and Late Application), with 20 EU + 10 non-EU applicants admitted in the Early Bird session and 21 EU applicants admitted in the Late session. The 2026/27 admission-information and brochure PDFs are live with 'Latest update: 21.05.2026'. IMPORTANT TIMING NOTE for a reader consulting this record on 2026-08-29: the 2026/27 intake is effectively CLOSED — the Early Bird window (02/03-28/04/2026) and the Late window (28/05-20/08/2026) have both expired; only enrolment formalities (until 13/10/2026, with late enrolment by 11/12/2026 if places remain) are still running. A new applicant would be targeting the 2027/28 cycle, whose dates are not yet published. No Additional Application Session ranking list for this programme existed on the ranking-lists index as of 2026-08-29.
is_new_programme: NOT a new programme. It is an established inter-university master run jointly with the University of Trento, with a documented teaching history: unibz publishes a 'Grade statistics LM-30' page for it showing a mature distribution of exam grades and, critically, a distribution of FINAL GRADUATION grades (most frequent final marks 103 at 15%, 110 cum laude at 15%, 102 at 12.50%, 104 at 10%, 107 at 10%, range from 98 to 110 cum laude) — i.e. cohorts have already graduated. Student representatives are named on the Course Council (Maddalena Svaldi and Stefano Tasin, supported by Farahi Mohammad Arif), another sign of an established programme. It is not flagged as 'new' anywhere on unibz.it, unlike e.g. the Bachelor in Informatics and Management of Digital Business. [uncertain] The exact first year of activation is not stated on any unibz.it page checked. What IS new for 2026/27 is the internal structure: the second year is now organised into two named curricula (see majors_tracks_study_plans), which reads as a recent restructuring rather than a new programme.
majors_tracks_study_plans: One admission route, then a CURRICULUM CHOICE IN THE SECOND YEAR (no separate application, no separate quota, no separate admission code — you apply to the programme, not to a curriculum). Year 1 is common: 'a core set of fundamental courses designed to build a solid foundation in energy engineering. Key topics include an overview of conventional and renewable energy resources, the principles and technologies behind the management and operation of energy conversion plants, and the analysis of energy use across major application sectors, such as residential and commercial buildings.' Year 2 offers two curricula: (1) 'Technologies for Energy Efficiency' — 'equips students with the skills to analyse, design, and optimise energy consumption in end-use applications, such as buildings, industrial processes, and distribution networks'; (2) 'Renewable and Innovative Technologies for Energy Supply' — 'focuses on the study and application of advanced technologies for producing and managing energy from renewable sources, like water, wind, and biomass'. 'Both curricula prepare students to address current and future challenges in sustainable energy systems.' Separately, there are two DOUBLE DEGREE tracks, joined after enrolment rather than at admission: with Universitat Politecnica de Catalunya, Barcelona (Spain) and with IMT Atlantique, Nantes (France). Internships with public or private energy companies in the region or abroad, plus exchange programmes with partner universities worldwide, are available. [uncertain] The double-degree selection procedure, quotas, deadlines and any additional language requirements (Spanish/French/Catalan) are not published on the unibz programme page; the curriculum-level course lists and their Bolzano/Trento location split are likewise not published statically.
english_only_accessibility: OPEN — one of the most accessible programmes at unibz for a candidate whose only European language is English. Rationale: (a) the sole language requirement is English B2 at entry ('Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2'); (b) there is NO German or Italian entry requirement, NO third-language B1 threshold and NO exit/graduation language requirement — the unibz Study Guide confirms the C1/C1/B1 graduation model applies only to TRILINGUAL master programmes, and that an entirely English-taught master 'does not include language requirements in other languages'; (c) all admission documents (CV, transcripts, the mandatory Excel file, the optional video) are submitted in English; (d) the optional video presentation is explicitly 'Language: English'. CAVEATS that temper the 'open' rating: (i) any oral interview covers applied thermodynamics, heat transfer, electrical engineering and fluid machinery — it is a technical, not a language, barrier, but it is conducted in English; (ii) the CURRICULAR ECTS requirement (24 maths + 16 chemistry/physics + 45 engineering ECTS for non-L-7/L-8/L-9 degrees) is the real filter, and it is far more restrictive than any language rule; (iii) part of the programme sits in Trento, a monolingual Italian city with no bilingual public administration, so daily life outside the classroom will be harder in Italian-only settings than in bilingual Bolzano; (iv) 'Optional courses could be offered also in Italian and German', so the elective menu is narrower for an English-only student. COMPETITION CAVEAT for non-EU applicants: in the 2026/27 Early Bird session 10 non-EU applicants were admitted and 15 more sat on the waiting list (ranks 11-25) — i.e. at least 25 eligible non-EU candidates chased 10 places, and non-EU applicants get ONE window only, with no Late or Additional session.
admission_type: RESTRICTED ACCESS (numero programmato / limited places), selected by a scored ranking list. There is NO written entrance exam, NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO GRE/GMAT and NO portfolio. The components are: (1) DOCUMENT-BASED SELECTION — the Admission Committee scores the file out of 100 points (CV + programme fit, personal preparation, English above B2, optional video); (2) CURRICULAR-REQUIREMENT CHECK — verification of the ECTS/SSD credit thresholds and the 22/30 minimum bachelor average; (3) AN ORAL INTERVIEW — conditional in general, but demonstrably MANDATORY in practice for at least some candidates: the 2026/27 Early Bird non-EU ranking list states that excluded applicants failed 'because they did not meet the admission requirements or they did not participate in the mandatory interview'; (4) A MANDATORY STRUCTURED EXCEL FILE — 'Applications without a completed excel file will not be considered'; (5) AN ELIGIBILITY THRESHOLD — 'Candidates awarded a score of 50/100 or more will be declared eligible for the programme and ranked accordingly'; (6) A LANGUAGE GATE — B2 English, failure of which means exclusion from the admission procedure regardless of score; (7) AN OPTIONAL VIDEO PRESENTATION (max 3 minutes, YouTube unlisted link) worth up to 10 points. Application is made online through the unibz Application Portal at https://aws.unibz.it/exup . Tie-break rule: 'In case of candidates having the same score, priority will be given to the youngest applicant.'
academic_requirements:
FOUR ALTERNATIVE QUALIFICATION ROUTES (admission-information PDF and both signed ranking lists, identical wording): '1. a bachelor degree in the Italian degree classes L-7 (Civil and Environmental Engineering), L-8 (Information Technology Engineering) or L-9 (Industrial Engineering) M.D. 1648/2023 (and ex M.D. 270/04); 2. a bachelor degree in the Italian degree classes 8, 9 and 10 ex M.D 509/99; 3. a bachelor degree in a class other than the above, university diploma or other qualification awarded abroad and recognised as suitable; 4. degree in a different category from those mentioned above, provided that a certain number of credits (ECTS) are earned in the following subject areas, at least equal to:' 

ROUTE 4 — THE CURRICULAR ECTS/SSD THRESHOLDS (this is the route most foreign applicants are assessed against; SSD codes are given in the NEW post-2024-reform format with the OLD code in brackets): 

MINIMUM 24 ECTS in mathematics/statistics areas: MATH-02/B (ex MAT/03) Geometry; MATH-03/A (ex MAT/05) Mathematical analysis; MATH-03/B (ex MAT/06) Probability and mathematical statistics; MATH-04/A (ex MAT/07) Mathematical physics; MATH-05/A (ex MAT/08) Numerical analysis; MATH-06/A (ex MAT/09) Operational research; STAT-01/B (ex SECS-S/02) Statistics for experimental and technological research. 

MINIMUM 16 ECTS in chemistry/physics/materials areas: CHEM-03/A (ex CHIM/03) General and inorganic chemistry; CHEM-05/A (ex CHIM/06) Organic chemistry; CHEM-06/A (ex CHIM/07) Chemical foundations of technologies; PHYS-01/A (ex FIS/01) Experimental physics of fundamental interactions and applications; PHYS-03/A (ex FIS/01 and FIS/03) Experimental physics of matter and applications; PHYS-04/A (ex FIS/03) Theoretical physics of matter, models, mathematical methods and application; IMAT-01/A (ex ING-IND/22) Materials science and technology. 

MINIMUM 45 ECTS in engineering areas: IIND-06/A (ex ING-IND/08) Fluid machinery; IIND-06/B (ex ING-IND/09) Energy systems and power generation; IIND-07/A (ex ING-IND/10) Thermal engineering and industrial energy systems; IIND-07/B (ex ING-IND/11) Building physics and building energy systems; IMIS-01/A (ex ING-IND/12) Mechanical and thermal measurements; IIND-02/A (ex ING-IND/13) Applied mechanics; IIND-03/B (ex ING-IND/15) Design methods for industrial engineering; IIND-04/A (ex ING-IND/16) Manufacturing technologies and systems; IIND-05/A (ex ING-IND/17) Industrial mechanical plants; ICHI-01/B (ex ING-IND/24) Fundamentals of chemical engineering; ICHI-02/A (ex ING-IND/25) Chemical plants; IIET-01/A (ex ING-IND/31) Electrical engineering; IIND-08/A (ex ING-IND/32) Power electronic converters, electrical machines and drives; IIND-08/B (ex ING-IND/33) Electrical power systems; CEAR-01/A (ex ICAR/01) Hydraulics; CEAR-01/B (ex ICAR/02) Hydrology and hydraulic and maritime structures; CEAR-02/A (ex ICAR/03) Sanitary and environmental engineering; CEAR-04/A (ex ICAR/06) Geomatics; CEAR-06/A (ex ICAR/08) Mechanics of solids and structures; CEAR-10/A (ex ICAR/17) Drawing; IIND-03/A (ex ING-IND/14) Mechanical design and machine construction. 

FLEXIBILITY CLAUSE: 'If you do not meet the requirements in point 4, the Admissions Committee may also consider credits from other subject areas if they are similar in content.' 

MINIMUM GRADE: 'The minimum average grade required in the bachelor's degree (excluding the final exam) is 22/30 (according to the Italian grading system).' Note this is the AVERAGE OF EXAMS, explicitly EXCLUDING the final/thesis exam, and it is expressed on the Italian 18-30 scale, so a foreign transcript must be converted. 

FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS: 'In case of foreign qualifications, the evaluation of the curricular requirements is made by the Admissions Committee that will assess the equivalence between the contents of the courses attended in previous careers and the subject areas of the programme.' The Faculty 'reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary'. 

ADEQUACY OF PERSONAL PREPARATION (a separate, additional hurdle on top of the curricular requirements): 'to be admitted to the master programme, you must show adequate preparation. This will be checked based on previous academic results and an interview, following the rules set out in the programme's study regulation.' It is deemed fulfilled if AT LEAST ONE of three criteria is met — see selection_scoring. 

AT ENROLMENT the Diploma Supplement must show 'that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS)' and 'that the qualification gives access to a Master programme'. 

DOUBLE-ENROLMENT RULE: a maximum of two simultaneous programmes, which 'must not belong to the same class, e.g., LM-30/LM-30' and (per the ranking lists) 'must differ for at least 2/3 of the course activities'. 

PRACTICAL READING FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT: a Turkish 4-year Makine Muhendisligi / Enerji Sistemleri Muhendisligi / Elektrik-Elektronik / Insaat / Cevre Muhendisligi bachelor normally satisfies routes 3 and 4 comfortably; a Fizik, Kimya, Matematik or Enerji Yonetimi background will be assessed strictly against the 24/16/45 ECTS grid and is where applications typically fail. The 22/30 floor corresponds roughly to a Turkish 4.00-scale GPA in the low-to-mid 2s, but unibz publishes no official Turkish conversion table.
selection_scoring:
A TWO-STAGE RUBRIC: first a pass/fail check of 'adequacy of personal preparation', then a 100-point score with a 50-point eligibility threshold. 

STAGE 1 — ADEQUACY OF PERSONAL PREPARATION (pass/fail; verbatim): 'The adequacy of personal preparation is considered fulfilled if at least one of the following criteria is met: a) Achievement of a Bachelor's degree grade equal to or greater than 100/110 (or an equivalent score for foreign qualifications) according to the information uploaded in the Excel file. b) Completion of at least 80% of the ECTS credits of the first-level degree programme with a weighted average grade equal to or greater than 26/30 (or an equivalent score for foreign qualifications). c) Successful performance in an oral interview aimed at verifying basic knowledge in applied thermodynamics, heat transfer, electrical engineering, and fluid machinery.' Note these are ALTERNATIVES ('at least one'): a strong graduate (>=100/110 final mark, or >=26/30 weighted average over >=80% of credits) can clear this stage on paper without an interview; a weaker one must pass the interview. 

STAGE 0 — SEPARATE MINIMUM GRADE GATE: 'The minimum average grade required in the bachelor's degree (excluding the final exam) is 22/30 (according to the Italian grading system).' This 22/30 is a hard curricular floor and is DISTINCT from the 26/30 in criterion (b), which is only one of the routes through the personal-preparation check. 

STAGE 2 — THE 100-POINT SCORE (verbatim): 'The evaluation is carried out by allocating points (max. 100) in accordance with the following criteria: a) Curriculum vitae (evaluation of the previous first-level university career, including educational and academic activities, as well as professional experiences) and consistency between the obtained qualification and the objectives of the Master's degree program in Energy Engineering (max. 50 points); b) Evaluation of personal preparation (final degree grade, GPA, and, if applicable, an interview) (max. 30 points); c) Further language competences in English if the level is higher than B2 (max. 10 points); d) video presentation (optional) (max. 3 minutes) (max. 10 points).' 

GATING RULE ON THE VIDEO (verbatim): 'The presentation video will only be evaluated if a minimum overall score between points a. and b. established by the commission is achieved. This is because candidates who do not obtain a minimum overall score in the first two points will not be able to mathematically achieve the 50/100 eligibility threshold, even if they obtain the maximum score in the video evaluation.' (a+b = 80 points maximum, c+d = 20; so a candidate scoring below 30 on a+b cannot reach 50 even with a perfect c+d, which is the arithmetic behind the rule.) 

THRESHOLD (verbatim): 'Candidates awarded a score of 50/100 or more will be declared eligible for the programme and ranked accordingly.' 

TIE-BREAK (verbatim): 'In case of candidates having the same score, priority will be given to the youngest applicant.' 

STRATEGIC READING: half the score (50/100) rides on CV quality and, crucially, FIT — 'consistency between the obtained qualification and the objectives of the Master's degree program in Energy Engineering'. This is where an applicant with a directly energy-related bachelor, an energy-related thesis and relevant internships gains the most. Only 10 points come from English above B2, so a C1/C2 certificate is a marginal, not a decisive, gain. 
[uncertain] The Committee's internal minimum on a+b that unlocks video scoring is 'established by the commission' and is not published. Individual applicants' scores are not published in the ranking lists (only applicant IDs), so no historical cut-off score can be derived.
bonus_points:
NO WEBOMETRICS UNIVERSITY-RANKING BONUS. This is a key difference from the unibz Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science, which award 3/2/1 points for a bachelor from a university in the Webometrics top 1000 / 1001-2000 / 2001-3000. No such clause appears in the Energy Engineering admission information or in either signed ranking list. 
NO GMAT/GRE BONUS (that is the Master in Accounting and Finance) and NO startup-project bonus (that is the Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation). 
The only score-boosting elements that function like bonuses are already inside the 100-point rubric: (1) ENGLISH ABOVE B2 — 'Further language competences in English if the level is higher than B2 (max. 10 points)', i.e. a C1 or C2 certificate (IELTS 7.0+, TOEFL iBT 95+, Cambridge C1 Advanced, etc.) is worth up to 10 points, while B2 exactly is worth zero on this line; (2) THE OPTIONAL VIDEO PRESENTATION — up to 10 points, but only scored if the CV+preparation subtotal clears the Committee's internal minimum; (3) A POST-GRADUATE QUALIFICATION ALREADY HELD — applicants may upload 'any other certificate of post-graduate Diploma (Master's degree) already awarded when submitting the application and including final grade, credits and marks achieved in each subject and GPA', which feeds the CV line (max 50) rather than a separate bonus. 
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE also counts, since the CV line explicitly covers 'professional experiences'.
portfolio_and_materials:
NO PORTFOLIO AND NO MOTIVATION LETTER are required — the materials package is transcript-driven. What must or may be uploaded: 

MANDATORY: 
(1) QUALIFICATION EVIDENCE — if graduated in Italy: diploma supplement or a self-declaration under D.P.R. no. 445/2000 stating the degree awarded with final grade and passed exams; if not yet graduated: a certificate listing exams passed. If graduated abroad: diploma supplement or final degree certificate with the passed exams; if not yet graduated: a transcript of records — in Italian, German or English. These must contain: 'final grade, exams passed with grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles)'. For foreign qualifications, additionally 'scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable)' — a detail applicants routinely omit and get excluded for. 
(2) THE EXCEL FILE — 'Please use the file available in the application portal. Applications without a completed excel file will not be considered.' This is the structured study-career template in which the applicant maps their own exams onto the SSD subject areas and states their grades; the Committee reads criterion (a) of the personal-preparation check 'according to the information uploaded in the Excel file'. It is a hard knock-out condition. 
(3) CURRICULUM VITAE — 'Curriculum vitae (in English)'. It carries up to 50 of the 100 points, so it is the single highest-value document. 
(4) A VALID ID CARD OR PASSPORT (front/back) at account creation — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'. 

OPTIONAL (score-bearing): 
(5) THE VIDEO PRESENTATION — worth up to 10 points. Official guidelines (LM-30 video presentation form): 'Maximum duration: 3 minutes. Language: English.' It must include 'Your full name; A brief introduction (your degree, a short description of your dissertation topic, and any relevant personal experiences); Academic reasons explaining how your university background is suited to the Master's programme you are applying for; Any other information that may support your admission.' Submission mechanics: 'Upload the video to YouTube as unlisted (it will be accessible only to those with the link). Then, include the link (copy/paste) when completing the online application form.' unibz even gives production tips: neutral background (plain wall or bookcase), frame the upper torso with headroom, camera about an arm's length away, good lighting without face shadows, rehearse to finish within 2 minutes 45 seconds, count silently to three after pressing record, and record two or three versions. 
(6) ANY POST-GRADUATE DIPLOMA / MASTER'S DEGREE already awarded, with final grade, credits, per-subject marks and GPA — 'an official translation of the transcript of records is required when the original document is not produced in English or Italian'. 

FORMAT LIMITS: unibz publishes no MB cap or page limit for these documents (unlike the 20 MB PDF portfolio cap in the Design programmes); the only stated limits are the video's 3 minutes and the English-language requirement for the CV and video.
interview:
YES — an oral interview is a formal part of the procedure, and for non-EU applicants it has operated as compulsory. 
SUBJECT MATTER (verbatim): 'an oral interview aimed at verifying basic knowledge in applied thermodynamics, heat transfer, electrical engineering, and fluid machinery.' 
WHEN IT APPLIES: (a) as one of the three alternative routes through the 'adequacy of personal preparation' check — needed by candidates who do not already hold a final bachelor mark of >=100/110 or a >=26/30 weighted average over >=80% of credits; (b) whenever the file is insufficient — 'In case the documents included in the online application do not allow the Admission Committee to adequately evaluate the application, the candidate might be asked to send further documentation (e.g. programmes of the courses taken) and/or to participate in an interview (in person or via videoconference)'; (c) in practice for non-EU applicants — the 2026/27 Early Bird non-EU ranking list states that excluded applicants 'did not meet the admission requirements or they did not participate in the mandatory interview'. 
FORMAT: in person or via videoconference; conducted in English. It also feeds the scored rubric, since line b) of the 100-point scale is 'Evaluation of personal preparation (final degree grade, GPA, and, if applicable, an interview) (max. 30 points)'. 
PROCEDURAL RULES: governed by 'the rules set out in the programme's study regulation'. 
[uncertain] NO INTERVIEW DATES ARE PUBLISHED for this programme anywhere on unibz.it — unlike, for example, the Master in Computing for Data Science, which publishes fixed interview dates. Candidates are convoked individually by e-mail after the application deadline and before the ranking-list publication date (so, for Early Bird 2026/27, somewhere between 28/04/2026 and 27/05/2026; for Late, between 20/08/2026 and 03/09/2026). The interview duration is also not published for this programme (the sister Master in Industrial Mechanical Engineering states 15-30 minutes, online, in English — a reasonable but unconfirmed analogue).
conditional_admission:
YES — conditional (provisional) admission for not-yet-graduated applicants is explicitly available and is heavily used in practice. 
RULE (verbatim): 'If you have not yet graduated at the time of application: Until your graduation, you will be admitted conditionally. You must complete your degree by the enrolment deadline. Otherwise, you will be excluded.' 
NOTE THE DIFFERENCE FROM UNIBZ BACHELOR PROGRAMMES: this master sets NO minimum-ECTS threshold to apply while still studying — there is no '>=120 ECTS' or '>=140 ECTS' condition of the kind the Master in Data Analytics for Economics and Management applies. The only condition is finishing by the enrolment deadline. 
DEADLINE FOR 2026/27: graduation must be completed by 13 October 2026, 12:00 midday (the enrolment deadline). 
SAFETY VALVE (verbatim advice from unibz): 'Advice: If you achieve your qualification after the enrolment deadline, you should not pay the tuition fees to confirm the study place. You will be able to submit a late enrolment request and, only if there are study places still available, you can enrol by 11 December 2026.' The ranking lists specify the late enrolment request goes 'to the Rector'. 
HOW COMMON IT IS: in the 2026/27 ranking lists, provisionally-admitted (not-yet-graduated) applicants are asterisked. Early Bird EU: 9 of the 20 admitted were asterisked. Early Bird non-EU: 3 of the 10 admitted. Late Application EU: 16 of the 21 admitted — i.e. the Late session is overwhelmingly used by candidates finishing their bachelor over the summer. 
A SECOND, SEPARATE FORM OF RESERVATION applies to foreign qualifications: 'Applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their study title can be verified' and 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded.' All non-EU citizens living abroad are additionally 'provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz'. 
FINAL WARNING: 'If you have been admitted in the ranking list, but you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.'
ofa_rules:
NOT APPLICABLE. OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning requirements) is an Italian instrument reserved for FIRST-CYCLE (bachelor) open-access programmes where an applicant fails a compulsory entrance test — at unibz it is used in the Bachelor in Economics and Management, the Bachelor in Economics, Politics and Ethics and the Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management (mathematics test), and OFA flags appear in bachelor ranking lists. No OFA clause exists for this master: neither the 2026/27 admission-information PDF, the brochure, nor either signed ranking list mentions OFA, additional learning requirements or remedial obligations, and the 2026/27 Energy Engineering ranking lists carry no OFA markers (their only asterisk denotes not-yet-graduated provisional admission). 
The functional master-level equivalents of OFA are instead handled BEFORE admission, not after: the curricular ECTS/SSD thresholds (24/16/45), the 22/30 minimum bachelor average and the 'adequacy of personal preparation' check with its oral interview. Italian law does not permit conditional master admission with credit debts to be resolved after enrolment in the way OFA works for bachelors — the curricular gaps must be closed before admission, typically by taking single supplementary courses ('corsi singoli') elsewhere first.
language_requirements:
SINGLE REQUIREMENT: ENGLISH AT B2 (CEFR) FOR ADMISSION. Verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2. The levels of the Common European Framework of Reference apply.' 
There is NO German requirement, NO Italian requirement, NO third-language B1 threshold and NO graduation/exit language requirement — this is a fully English-taught master, not a trilingual programme. 
THE LANGUAGE GATE IS A HARD KNOCK-OUT: failure to prove B2 means exclusion from the admission procedure regardless of academic score. (Across unibz, this gate is the single most common cause of exclusion — for the trilingual Bachelor in Computer Science, all 26 non-EU applicants in the 2026/27 Early Bird session were excluded for language. For this English-only master the gate is far easier to clear, which is precisely why it is a good target for an English-speaking international applicant.) 
WHERE TO PROVE IT: in the Application Portal, sections 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams', which become available only AFTER creating an application under 'create/manage applications'. 
ADMINISTRATIVE FORM: 'In case your final certificate has been awarded by an Italian public institution, you need to submit a self-declaration. In case your final certificate has been awarded by a foreign public institution, you need to upload diploma scanned copy of the original.' 
SCORING BONUS: English ABOVE B2 is worth up to 10 of the 100 selection points, so a C1/C2 certificate is worth obtaining even though B2 suffices for admission. 
DEADLINE MECHANICS: certificates that cannot be uploaded may be e-mailed as PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre BY THE APPLICATION DEADLINE.
entry_levels_by_position:
ENGLISH B2 / no 2nd language / no 3rd language — i.e. in unibz's positional notation, B2 / none / none. 
unibz expresses language requirements by POSITION (1st, 2nd, 3rd teaching language) rather than by named language. For this programme there is only ONE teaching language, English, in first position at B2. No level is required in a second or third language at any stage, because the programme is not trilingual. 
Comparison across unibz to place this correctly: trilingual engineering bachelors run B2/B2/none (Bachelor in Computer Science) or B2/B1/none (Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering); trilingual masters in Economics run C1/B2/none (Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance, Master in Accounting and Finance). Against those, Energy Engineering's single B2-in-English requirement is the least demanding language profile available at unibz and is what makes the programme genuinely open to English-only candidates. 
The only nuance: 'Optional courses could be offered also in Italian and German', so choosing certain electives may in practice presuppose Italian or German — but no CEFR level is formally required for any of them.
exit_levels:
NO EXIT / GRADUATION LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT. The unibz Study Guide's language model draws an explicit line: the C1/C1/B1 graduation model applies to TRILINGUAL master programmes ('in order to graduate, you will need to certify two languages at the C1 level and the third language at the B1 level'), whereas for an English-taught master it states that the programme 'is entirely in English and does not include language requirements in other languages', with Language Centre courses offered as an optional extra rather than an obligation. 
Neither the 2026/27 admission-information PDF, the brochure, nor either signed ranking list states any exit level for this programme — the 'Language requirements' section covers ENTRY ONLY. 
PRACTICAL SIGNIFICANCE: this removes the single biggest hidden risk of studying at unibz for an international student. In the trilingual programmes, students routinely gain admission and then cannot graduate on time because they have not certified the second and third languages. Here, once admitted with B2 English, no further language certification stands between the student and the degree. 
Students may still voluntarily take unibz Language Centre courses in German or Italian, which is worth doing for the Bolzano/Trento job market, but it carries no graduation consequence.
third_language_exam_threshold:
NOT APPLICABLE — there is no third language, therefore no third-language B1 threshold. 
The rule this field is designed to capture (a B1 level in the third language required from the second semester of the first year in order to be allowed to sit exams) belongs to unibz's TRILINGUAL programmes. It does not appear in the Energy Engineering 2026/27 admission-information PDF, brochure or either signed ranking list, and it cannot apply to a programme whose 'official teaching language is English' full stop. 
There is likewise no first-language or second-language exam threshold gating exam attendance. The only language condition attached to this programme is the B2 English entry gate, which is settled before admission. 
The unibz Study Guide's 'Trilingual master programmes' page (C1/C1/B1 to graduate) is the page that does NOT govern this programme; the governing page is 'English-taught master programmes'.
proof_pathways:
FOUR RECOGNISED WAYS TO PROVE ENGLISH B2 (admission-information PDF, verbatim numbering): 
(1) MEDIUM OF INSTRUCTION AT HIGH SCHOOL — 'the main teaching language in your final high school year, if English (recognised as C1). Foreign qualifications: If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your high school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction.' Note this is recognised at C1, not merely B2, so it ALSO earns points on the 'English above B2' line of the rubric. 
(2) A DEGREE TAUGHT IN ENGLISH — 'a bachelor or master degree in English (recognised as C1). unibz graduates must upload the language certificates obtained and/or declare that they have passed language exams at the unibz Language Centre (B2, B2+ or C1). Foreign qualifications: If the teaching language is not clearly stated on your University degree, please also upload a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction during your studies.' This is the most common route for international applicants and is also recognised at C1. Turkish applicants from 100%-English-medium programmes (e.g. METU, Bogazici, ITU English-track, Bilkent, Koc, Sabanci) should obtain a formal medium-of-instruction letter from the registrar, since Turkish diplomas usually do not state the language. Applicants from 30%-English Turkish programmes should NOT rely on this route. 
(3) A RECOGNISED LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE — from the official unibz list. 'If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.' 
(4) A UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE EXAM — 'You can register for these exams online through the application portal (in the section "enrol for language exams") after you have filled out your application in the section "create/manage applications".' Held ONLINE. 2026/27 sittings and registration windows — Early Bird: exam 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and exams 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late: exams 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026) and 27/07/2026 (registration 10-19/07/2026). CRITICAL PROCEDURAL TRAP (verbatim): 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.' 
RECOMMENDATION: routes (1) and (2) are strictly better than (3) and (4) where available, because they are recognised as C1 and therefore also feed the up-to-10-point 'English above B2' bonus.
certificate_rules:
Governed by the unibz list of recognised language certificates (Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026, 'Recognised language certificates and diplomas — Students and applicants'). 
B2 ENGLISH EQUIVALENCES from the official table (the level this programme needs): IELTS (General and Academic) 5.5-6.5; TOEFL iBT 72-94; Cambridge B2 First (FCE) grade B or C, and B2 First for Schools; Cambridge B1 Business Preliminary / BEC Vantage grade B or C; TOEIC Listening 400+, Reading 385+, Speaking 160+, Writing 150+; PTE Academic 43-58; PTE General Level 3; PEIC B2; LanguageCert General B2 / LanguageCert Academic B2 / LanguageCert ESOL B2; Michigan English Test (MET) B2 (all 4 skills); Aptis ESOL General B2 and Aptis ESOL Advanced B2. 
FOR THE 'ABOVE B2' BONUS (up to 10 points), C1 equivalences include: IELTS 7.0-8.0; TOEFL iBT 95-113; Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE); BEC Higher grade B/C; TOEIC Listening 490+, Reading 455+, Speaking 180+, Writing 180+; PTE Academic 59-75 (C1 band per the table's column ordering); LanguageCert C1; MET C1; Aptis ESOL Advanced C1. C2: IELTS 8.5+, TOEFL iBT 114-120, Cambridge C2 Proficiency (CPE), ECPE, PEIC C2, PTE Academic 85-90. 
GENERAL RULES: (1) the certificate must assess ALL FOUR SKILLS and be issued by the certification organisation itself; (2) an overall grade must be shown, or the detailed per-skill assessment must appear on the certificate or in documentation from the issuer; (3) if no overall level is stated, THE LOWEST LEVEL REACHED IN ANY SUB-SKILL determines the recognised level; (4) there is NO COMPENSATION between skills and no averaging unless the issuer itself provides it; (5) 'Certificates regarding single skills issued by different certification organisations will not be accepted'; (6) certificates of participation, end-of-course tests, exams from private educational institutions, placement-test results and certificates issued by individual lecturers are NOT recognised; (7) DAAD certificates are NOT recognised. 
HOME EDITION: online 'home edition' exams are generally NOT recognised, EXCEPT those explicitly asterisked in the list. For English, the asterisk (footnote: 'Also accepted as "home edition"') covers TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS (General and Academic) and LanguageCert Academic — a significant practical advantage for candidates in Turkey and other countries where at-home testing is common. 
VALIDITY: 'International language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of their submission. The entire calendar year shall apply from 1 January.' The list repeats: 'Only certificates taken in the past 5 years are recognized.' Items under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' (including a unibz bachelor or master degree issued under the university's language policy) have UNLIMITED validity. 
Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf

application_deadline_non_eu:
ONE WINDOW ONLY, NO SECOND CHANCE: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28 (Early Bird), by noon local Italian time on the closing day. Verbatim: 'Non-EU-Citizens (living outside of Italy): Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' 
This is the single most important planning fact for a Turkish, Indian, Iranian, Pakistani or other non-EU applicant who does not hold a qualifying Italian residence permit: miss 28 April and the academic year is gone. There is no Late Application and no Additional Session for this category — the Late ranking list for 2026/27 is headed 'EU CITIZENS AND CITIZEN ENJOYING PARITY OF TREATMENT' only. 
An application fee of EUR 50 applies to this category only, and it is non-refundable. 
DOWNSTREAM DEADLINES for a successful non-EU applicant (2026/27): ranking list by 2026-05-27; first instalment of EUR 600 to secure the place by 2026-06-05 noon; Universitaly pre-enrolment immediately afterwards (mandatory); visa application at the Italian consulate; enrolment 2026-07-10 to 2026-10-13 noon. The gap between securing the place in early June and the October enrolment deadline is the visa window, and it is tight — Italian consulates in high-demand countries book out months ahead, so the Universitaly pre-enrolment should be filed the same week the instalment is paid. 
WARNING ON CATEGORY ASSIGNMENT: 'if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad' — see parity_of_treatment.
parity_of_treatment:
TWO CATEGORIES ARE TREATED EXACTLY LIKE EU APPLICANTS (verbatim from the admission-information PDF): 
'1. Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State; 
2. Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: "permesso di soggiorno" (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay. A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid. If the permit has expired, you must attach a renewal request.'

WHY THIS MATTERS ENORMOUSLY FOR TURKISH APPLICANTS: category 2 is the third route that converts a Turkish citizen from the 10-place, single-window, EUR 50-fee, visa-dependent non-EU track onto the 40-place EU track with TWO application windows and no application fee. A Turkish national already living in Italy on a work, family-reunification, asylum or religious permit qualifies. A Turkish national on a STUDENT permit (e.g. currently doing an Italian bachelor) does NOT — this is the most common and most damaging misunderstanding. 

THE AUTOMATIC-DOWNGRADE TRAP (verbatim): 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' The signed ranking lists repeat it: 'If you have declared to be resident in Italy but have not attached to your application a copy of your valid residence permit for Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998) you are ranked together with the non-EU citizen resident abroad.' 

CONCRETE 2026/27 IMPACT: the EU/parity list had 20 places and 23 eligible candidates in Early Bird (plus 21 more admitted in Late), while the non-EU list had 10 places and at least 25 eligible candidates. Being on the parity track was therefore materially easier, and it also unlocked the Late Application session.
places_quotas:
50 PLACES IN TOTAL. Brochure 'At a glance': 'Places available: 40 EU + 10 Non-EU'. Broken down by session in the admission-information PDF, verbatim: 
'EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment — Early Bird Application: 20; Late Application: 20. Non-EU citizens (living abroad) — Early Bird Application: 10.' 
So: EU Early Bird 20 / EU Late 20 / non-EU 10 (Early Bird only). 
ROLLOVER RULE (verbatim): 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application.' Unused non-EU places do NOT roll over to EU applicants in any published rule, and unused EU places do not roll over to non-EU applicants. 

2026/27 OUTCOMES — the real competition picture (from the signed ranking lists): 
EARLY BIRD, EU/parity: exactly 20 admitted, plus a waiting list of 3 (ranks 21-23) => at least 23 eligible EU applicants for 20 places; oversubscription roughly 1.15x. Waiting-list candidates were told they 'will be contacted by e-mail as of 8 June 2026 in case a spot opens up'. 
EARLY BIRD, NON-EU LIVING ABROAD: 10 admitted, plus a waiting list of 15 (ranks 11-25) => at least 25 eligible non-EU applicants for 10 places; oversubscription roughly 2.5x, and that counts only those who cleared eligibility — others were excluded outright for failing requirements or for not attending the mandatory interview. 
LATE APPLICATION, EU only: 21 admitted, no waiting list published => the EU side effectively filled to 41 admissions across the two sessions against a 40-place EU quota (admissions exceed places because not every admitted candidate confirms; one applicant ID, 154323, appears in both lists). 

READING: for EU/parity candidates this is a mildly competitive programme where a decent file gets in; for non-EU candidates abroad it is genuinely competitive at about 2.5 eligible applicants per place, in a single annual window.

required_documents:
UPLOADED IN THE APPLICATION PORTAL (https://aws.unibz.it/exup) AT APPLICATION: 
(1) A VALID ID CARD OR PASSPORT, front and back, at account creation — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'. 
(2) QUALIFICATION DOCUMENTS. Graduated in Italy: diploma supplement or a D.P.R. 445/2000 self-declaration of the degree with final grade and passed exams; if not yet graduated, a certificate listing exams passed. Graduated abroad: diploma supplement or final degree certificate with passed exams; if not yet graduated, a transcript of records — in Italian, German or English. Must contain 'final grade, exams passed with grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles)', and for foreign qualifications also the 'scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable)'. If the qualification was gained abroad, the DIPLOMA must also be uploaded ('if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment'). 
(3) THE EXCEL FILE (structured study-career template) — 'Please use the file available in the application portal. Applications without a completed excel file will not be considered.' HARD KNOCK-OUT. 
(4) CURRICULUM VITAE IN ENGLISH. 
(5) LANGUAGE EVIDENCE — certificate, or medium-of-instruction documentation, or Language Centre exam registration. Italian public-institution certificates: self-declaration. Foreign public-institution certificates: scanned copy of the original. 
OPTIONAL, SCORE-BEARING: (6) the URL of a YouTube-unlisted video presentation of max 3 minutes; (7) any post-graduate diploma / master's degree already awarded, with final grade, credits, per-subject marks and GPA (official translation required if not in English or Italian). 
FOR PARITY-OF-TREATMENT APPLICANTS: (8) a copy of the valid Italian permesso di soggiorno (or the renewal request if expired) — without it the applicant is automatically ranked as non-EU abroad. 

ADDITIONALLY AT ENROLMENT, FOR FOREIGN DEGREES: the bachelor degree diploma; an official Italian translation (not needed if issued in German or English); the Diploma Supplement stating at least 180 ECTS achieved and that the qualification gives access to a master programme; plus the ARDI/CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. Transfer students from another Italian university must give the Student Office a copy of the transfer application filed at their university of origin at the start of the academic year. 

STANDING WARNING, repeated twice in the PDF: 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.' The Faculty may also request course content descriptions and/or teaching hours.
application_fee:

tuition_or_fees_link:
EUR 1,200 PER YEAR IN TOTAL, in two instalments. Verbatim: 'Fees amount to EUR 1200. 1st instalment (EUR 600): includes the revenue stamp of EUR 16. 2nd instalment (EUR 600): must be paid by March of the following year.' 
The first instalment is also the payment that SECURES an admitted place (Early Bird 2026/27 deadline 2026-06-05 noon; Late 2026-09-11 noon). 
unibz charges a FLAT FEE — it is NOT income-scaled (no ISEE-based brackets as at most Italian state universities), and non-EU students pay the same EUR 1,200 as EU students. Against the Italian and wider European market this is very low for an English-taught engineering master, which is a substantial part of the programme's value proposition. 
CONSEQUENCES OF NON-PAYMENT: 'Delayed payment of the second instalment will result in a fine being levied. If you have not paid the tuition fees, you will be unable to take exams and will not be able to transfer to other universities or other study programmes.' And: 'If you drop out of a programme, interrupt your studies or are excluded from studies, you are not entitled to reimbursement of the fees.' 
EXEMPTIONS: 'Students with a disability recognized under article 3, paragraph 1, of Law No 104/1992, or with a disability up to or exceeding 66%: the disability certificate, issued by the health authorities, must be handed in at the beginning of the academic year' and 'Foreign students who have been granted a scholarship from the Italian government'. 
REFUND FOR GRANT HOLDERS: 'Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to receive a refund of the tuition fees.' 
REFUND EXCEPTION FOR VISA FAILURE: non-EU applicants living abroad who pay but 'do not receive the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country' ARE entitled to a refund. 
Fees pages: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ and the programme's own admission-information PDF. 
NOT INCLUDED: living costs. Bolzano is among the most expensive Italian cities for housing, and the programme also involves time in Trento — budget both.
scholarships_grants:
NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC SCHOLARSHIP is published for the Master in Energy Engineering. The available routes are university-wide or provincial: 
(1) PROVINCIAL STUDY GRANT of the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano (Office for Higher Education Support / Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario), applied for online through the provincial e-government service, with help available from the South Tyrolean Students Association. The Province offers three instruments: ordinary study grants, merit scholarships, and grants for fostering postgraduate studies. Grant holders additionally 'receive the reimbursement of monies paid for the academic year', i.e. the EUR 1,200 tuition is refunded. 
CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS (verbatim): 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption.' A newly arrived non-EU first-year student is therefore effectively INELIGIBLE IN YEAR ONE and should budget accordingly, becoming eligible from the second year. Note also the geography problem: the grant is tied to residence in SOUTH TYROL, while part of this programme sits in Trento (a different autonomous province, Trentino), so students spending substantial time in Trento should verify how their residence is assessed. [uncertain] 
(2) UNIBZ TUITION-FEE EXEMPTIONS rather than cash: disability under Law 104/1992 art. 3(1) or >=66% disability; holders of an Italian government scholarship. 
(3) ITALIAN GOVERNMENT SCHOLARSHIPS for foreign students (MAECI 'Invest Your Talent in Italy' and the annual MAECI scholarship call) — external to unibz and applied for separately, typically in the spring. 
[uncertain] The frequently cited provincial grant range of roughly EUR 1,680-6,960 per year, and merit thresholds such as a 27/30 weighted average after the first year, could NOT be confirmed on the unibz pages verified for this programme; amounts and thresholds are set annually by the provincial call and must be checked directly.

credential_recognition:
AT ENROLMENT, a holder of a foreign bachelor degree must upload: the degree diploma; an official translation into Italian ('not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English'); and the DIPLOMA SUPPLEMENT, which must state 'that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS)' and 'that the qualification gives access to a Master programme'. Then, depending on the education system: 
(a) EU COUNTRIES, SWITZERLAND, NORWAY, ICELAND, LIECHTENSTEIN — 'the Statement of Correspondence of your Bachelor degree, to be downloaded from the ARDI - Automatic Recognition Database - Italy'. 
(b) NON-EU COUNTRIES THAT ARE SIGNATORIES TO THE LISBON CONVENTION — BOTH the ARDI Statement of Correspondence AND 'the Statement of Verification of your Bachelor degree, issued by the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence (CIMEA)'. 
(c) NON-EU COUNTRIES NOT SIGNATORIES TO THE LISBON CONVENTION — BOTH 'the Statement of Comparability ... issued by CIMEA' AND 'the Statement of Verification ... issued by CIMEA'. 

FOR TURKISH APPLICANTS: Turkiye IS a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish degrees normally fall under case (b) — ARDI Statement of Correspondence PLUS CIMEA Statement of Verification. Both take time and CIMEA charges a fee, so start immediately after the ranking list is published rather than waiting for the October enrolment deadline. 

RESERVATION AND REVOCATION: 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded. During enrolment, unibz verifies your foreign qualification and may request additional documents if necessary. If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' And: 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' 

SEPARATELY, AT ADMISSION (not enrolment), the ACADEMIC CONTENT of a foreign degree is judged by the Admission Committee itself: 'In case of foreign qualifications, the evaluation of the curricular requirements is made by the Admissions Committee that will assess the equivalence between the contents of the courses attended in previous careers and the subject areas of the programme.' This content assessment, driven by the mandatory Excel file, is what decides the 24/16/45 ECTS thresholds — ARDI/CIMEA statements do NOT substitute for it. 

RECOGNITION OF PRIOR CREDITS: 'Credit points from previous university studies can only be recognised after enrolment if the exams taken at the university of provenance are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz.'

SEQUENCE FOR A NON-EU CITIZEN LIVING ABROAD (2026/27 dates): 
(1) Apply to unibz in the EARLY BIRD WINDOW ONLY, 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28 noon, paying the EUR 50 application fee. There is no second window. 
(2) Appear on the SEPARATE NON-EU RANKING LIST (10 places), published by 2026-05-27. 
(3) SECURE THE PLACE by paying the EUR 600 first instalment by 2026-06-05 noon. 
(4) THEN PRE-ENROL ON UNIVERSITALY — mandatory and sequenced after payment. Verbatim: 'Once the ranking list has been published, if you have gained admission, secure it by paying the first instalment and then start your visa application on the Universitaly portal. The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' The ranking list is blunter: 'Should you not follow this procedure, your direct online application to unibz will be declared null and void.' 
(5) OBTAIN THE STUDY VISA from the Italian embassy/consulate in your country. Explicit caveat: 'preliminary admission by unibz does not guarantee obtaining a visa, the issuing of which is the exclusive responsibility of embassies and consulates. Likewise, obtaining a visa for study purposes does not confer any right to perfecting the enrolment in a study programme.' 
(6) ENROL ONLINE between 2026-07-10 and 2026-10-13 noon. 
(7) AFTER ARRIVAL: 'within 8 working days of your arrival in Italy, according to Italian law you must apply for a residence permit: as soon as you arrive, get in touch with the Student Support and you will be given the necessary information for starting the procedure.' Once the permesso di soggiorno is issued, 'you have to hand it in at the Student Office personally or via e-mail'. 
FINANCIAL MEANS FOR THE VISA: proof of at least EUR 800 per month for living costs excluding tuition, i.e. roughly EUR 24,000 total for a two-year master. Health insurance is required. [uncertain] — these figures come from unibz's general international-applicant material and the Italian ministerial circular, not from this programme's 2026/27 PDF; consulates set their own evidentiary standards. 
STUDENT WORK: limited to 20 hours per week / 1,040 hours per year. [uncertain] — general Italian rule, not restated in this programme's PDF. 
REFUND EXCEPTION: non-EU applicants abroad who pay the instalment but do not obtain the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country ARE entitled to a refund — the only refund route unibz grants. 
ADMISSION IS PROVISIONAL THROUGHOUT: 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.'

DATA YEAR: everything here is the 2026/27 cycle, from documents stamped 'Latest update: 21.05.2026' and marked 'Subject to change'. Read on 2026-08-29, the 2026/27 intake is effectively closed (both application windows have expired; only enrolment runs to 13/10/2026, with late enrolment to 11/12/2026). A prospective applicant is targeting 2027/28, whose dates, quotas and possibly rubric are NOT yet published. Treat every date here as an indicative pattern for 2027/28, not a commitment. 

RESOLVED CONTRADICTION: the brochure 'At a glance' says '40 EU + 10 Non-EU' while the detailed section lists EU Early Bird 20 + EU Late 20. These agree — 40 is the EU TOTAL across two sessions. An early automated read of the HTML page misreported '40 places (Early Bird) with additional 20 in Late'; that reading is WRONG and is corrected here against the PDF and the signed ranking lists. 

OPEN UNCERTAINTIES: 
(1) JOINT-DEGREE STATUS — unibz says only 'In collaboration with the University of Trento' and files the programme under 'Inter-university Masters'. Whether the parchment is a single joint degree, a double degree, or a unibz degree is not stated on unibz.it. Whether one can alternatively apply through UniTrento (with different quotas/deadlines) is likewise unstated; the UniTrento page (corsi.unitn.it/en/energy-engineering) blocked automated access, and the outline restricts sourcing to unibz.it. An applicant should e-mail engineering@unibz.it to confirm which university to apply to. 
(2) CAMPUS SPLIT — how the two years and two curricula divide between NOI Techpark Bolzano and Trento is not published; the programme page's 'Study course structure' widget loads dynamically and yielded no static course list. This has real housing and cost consequences and should be asked directly. 
(3) INTERVIEW LOGISTICS — no dates, no duration, no format details are published for this programme. The sister Master in Industrial Mechanical Engineering states 15-30 minutes, online, in English; that is a plausible but UNCONFIRMED analogue. The 'programme's study regulation' that governs the interview was not locatable in English on unibz.it. 
(4) THE COMMITTEE'S INTERNAL a+b MINIMUM that unlocks video scoring is 'established by the commission' and never published. 
(5) NO HISTORICAL CUT-OFF SCORE can be derived: ranking lists publish applicant IDs only, never scores. The 50/100 eligibility threshold is the only published number, and it is a floor, not the admission cut-off in an oversubscribed session. 
(6) DOUBLE DEGREE (UPC Barcelona / IMT Atlantique Nantes) — selection procedure, quotas, timing, credit arrangements and any Spanish/Catalan/French language requirements are not published on the unibz programme page. 
(7) SCHOLARSHIP AMOUNTS — the commonly cited EUR 1,680-6,960 provincial grant range and merit thresholds could not be confirmed; they are set annually by the provincial call. There is an unresolved question of how residence is assessed for students spending time in Trento (Trentino province) rather than South Tyrol. 
(8) VISA FINANCIAL THRESHOLDS (EUR 800/month, roughly EUR 24,000 for a master) and the 20 hours/week work limit come from unibz general material and Italian national rules, NOT from this programme's 2026/27 PDF. 
(9) FIRST YEAR OF ACTIVATION of the programme is not stated anywhere on unibz.it. 
(10) INFO SESSION DATES are 'to be defined' in the 21.05.2026 brochure. 
(11) The Italian and German editions of the admission-information PDF were not separately verified for divergence from the English text.
